_note: The named trains behind the rail atlas's 'Legendary Trains' view (t.world / t.train).
OURS, NOT THE API'S. Virtuoso's /v2/tours has no field for which train a journey
rides — travelStyles says 'Rail' and stops there. The scraped feed this atlas was
built from carried the name on 75 of its 135 journeys, and the migration to the API
dropped it, which emptied the Legendary Trains view and left every rail card without
its train. This ledger puts it back on the curation side of the line the whole
Virtuoso migration follows: the API owns facts, we own how they are grouped.
`match` is a case-insensitive regular expression tested against the tour's name, its
company and its description, IN THIS FILE'S ORDER — so the specific train wins over
its operator. 'Royal Scotsman, a Belmond Train' has to match Royal Scotsman, which is
only true while Belmond sits last.
The description is searched on purpose. Eleven Canadian journeys name neither train in
their title — 'Grand Canadian Train Journey | Vancouver to Halifax' — and say Rocky
Mountaineer or VIA Rail in the prose. Dropping those would lose the trips most people
mean when they ask about riding across Canada.
